url: /kuda/tutorials/first-run.md

# Tutorial: your first index

Goal: go from a checkout to a queryable memory in minutes.

## 1. Init

```sh
cd your-repo
kuda init
```

Detects languages from file extensions + manifests, writes a
commented `kuda.toml` and a `.kuda/` skeleton. Review the toml —
defaults (`manifest` + `treesitter` extract, `template` summarize,
`sqlite` store) are fully local and deterministic.

## 2. Sync

```sh
kuda sync
```

Hashes files, runs extractors, writes:

```
.kuda/index.yaml      L0 repo card  — commit this
.kuda/modules/*.yaml  L1 cards      — commit these
.kuda/index.sqlite    L2 graph      — gitignored, rebuildable
.kuda/meta.json       provenance    — sha + hashes
```

## 3. Query

```sh
kuda map                    # the card an agent would load
kuda card <module>          # purpose, api, deps, freshness
kuda find <symbol>          # symbol -> file:line
kuda dependents <symbol>    # who calls it — impact analysis
kuda refs <name> --docs     # code + docs/comments mentions
```

## 4. Stay fresh

```sh
kuda status   # "3/40 cards stale" — provenance sha vs HEAD
kuda sync     # regenerates only the drifted cards
```

Commit `index.yaml` + `modules/` — the prose is reviewable in diffs.

url: /kuda/how-to/multi-repo.md

# How-to: index a multi-repo workspace

For orgs spread across sibling checkouts (mono-repos too — a
workspace is just a set of roots).

## Workspace file

Create `.kuda/workspace.yaml` in the parent dir of your checkouts:

```yaml
roots:
  - platform
  - cli
  - lsp
  - kit-canonical
resolve_git_deps: true   # github.com/org/repo deps -> siblings
```

## Sync the workspace

```sh
kuda sync --workspace          # indexes every root
kuda dependents Foo --workspace # cross-repo reverse lookup
```

With `resolve_git_deps`, manifest edges like
`git = "https://github.com/org/cli"` resolve to the `../cli`
checkout — "X moved to the sibling repo" stops being prose-only
knowledge and becomes a graph edge.

## Tips

* Each repo keeps its own `kuda.toml` + `.kuda/`; the workspace
  layer only links them.
* Run `kuda status --workspace` after pulling several repos —
  it reports drift per repo.

url: /kuda/how-to/mcp.md
---
# How-to: serve the index over MCP

`kuda mcp` exposes the index as tools to MCP-capable agents
(Devin, Cursor, Claude Code, …).

## Run

```sh
kuda mcp             # stdio server, serves the repo's index
kuda mcp --workspace # all roots in .kuda/workspace.yaml
```

## Tools

| tool          | query                                    |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `repo_card`   | L0 blob — the always-load summary        |
| `module_card` | L1 card + freshness for one module       |
| `find`        | symbol -> file:line                      |
| `dependents`  | reverse dep edges (impact analysis)      |
| `refs`        | code + docs/comments mentions            |
| `status`      | provenance drift vs HEAD                 |

## Register with your agent

Point the agent's MCP config at `kuda mcp` (stdio). Exact config
shape depends on the client — see your client's MCP docs.

## Trust model

Cards are hypotheses. Every `module_card` response includes the
`verify:` file list — agents should open those files before
acting on card content. `status` tells them whether the whole
index drifted.

---

---
url: /kuda/how-to/llm-summarizer.md
---
# How-to: opt into the LLM summarizer

The default `template` summarizer is deterministic and zero-model —
cards contain only what extraction found (APIs, deps, commands).
The `llm` adapter adds prose: purpose, invariants, "who calls me".

## Enable

```toml
# kuda.toml
[summarize]
kind = "llm"
provider = "anthropic"
# model = "..."
```

Set the key — never in the toml:

```sh
export KUDA_LLM_KEY=...   # or: kuda secret set KUDA_LLM_KEY
```

Resolution order: env var -> OS keyring -> `~/.config/kuda/env`.

## Grounding rules (enforced by the adapter)

* Cards must cite the files they summarize — emitted as the
  `verify:` list.
* No invented APIs: every symbol in a card must resolve in the
  index.
* `notes:` regions are human-owned — regen never overwrites them.

## Cost control

Summaries regenerate only when a card's `files` change
(content-hash invalidation) — `sync` stays cheap; `--full`
re-summarizes everything.

# Command-Line Help for `kuda`

This document contains the help content for the `kuda` command-line program.

**Command Overview:**

* [`kuda`↴](#kuda)
* [`kuda init`↴](#kuda-init)
* [`kuda sync`↴](#kuda-sync)
* [`kuda status`↴](#kuda-status)
* [`kuda map`↴](#kuda-map)
* [`kuda card`↴](#kuda-card)
* [`kuda find`↴](#kuda-find)
* [`kuda dependents`↴](#kuda-dependents)
* [`kuda refs`↴](#kuda-refs)
* [`kuda mcp`↴](#kuda-mcp)
* [`kuda acp`↴](#kuda-acp)
* [`kuda doctor`↴](#kuda-doctor)

## `kuda`

A hippocampus for your codebase — repo memory: index, query, verify

**Usage:** `kuda [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

###### **Subcommands:**

* `init` — Detect languages -> kuda.toml + .kuda/ scaffold
* `sync` — Incremental index (hash -> extract -> summarize -> store)
* `status` — Provenance vs HEAD: per-card drift report
* `map` — Render the L0 repo card (the always-load blob)
* `card` — Module card + freshness
* `find` — Symbol -> file:line
* `dependents` — Reverse dep lookup — impact analysis
* `refs` — Code + docs/comments mentions — the doc-sweep query
* `mcp` — Serve the index over MCP (stdio)
* `acp` — Speak ACP — Agent Client Protocol surface for any agent client (zed, cline, cursor)
* `doctor` — Extractor/store/config health

###### **Options:**

* `--config <CONFIG>` — Config path (else $KUDA_CONFIG, ./kuda.toml, ~/.config/kuda/kuda.toml)
* `--workspace` — Workspace mode — all roots in .kuda/workspace.yaml

## `kuda init`

Detect languages -> kuda.toml + .kuda/ scaffold

**Usage:** `kuda init`

## `kuda sync`

Incremental index (hash -> extract -> summarize -> store)

**Usage:** `kuda sync [OPTIONS]`

###### **Options:**

* `--full` — Rebuild everything, ignoring content-hash freshness

## `kuda status`

Provenance vs HEAD: per-card drift report

**Usage:** `kuda status`

## `kuda map`

Render the L0 repo card (the always-load blob)

**Usage:** `kuda map`

## `kuda card`

Module card + freshness

**Usage:** `kuda card <MODULE>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<MODULE>`

## `kuda find`

Symbol -> file:line

**Usage:** `kuda find <SYMBOL>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<SYMBOL>`

## `kuda dependents`

Reverse dep lookup — impact analysis

**Usage:** `kuda dependents <NAME>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<NAME>`

## `kuda refs`

Code + docs/comments mentions — the doc-sweep query

**Usage:** `kuda refs [OPTIONS] <NAME>`

###### **Arguments:**

* `<NAME>`

###### **Options:**

* `--docs` — Only docs/comments/markdown mentions

## `kuda mcp`

Serve the index over MCP (stdio)

**Usage:** `kuda mcp`

## `kuda acp`

Speak ACP — Agent Client Protocol surface for any agent client (zed, cline, cursor)

**Usage:** `kuda acp`

## `kuda doctor`

Extractor/store/config health

**Usage:** `kuda doctor`

# Config — `kuda.toml`

## Top level

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repo` | `RepoCfg` | optional | — |
| `extract` | `ExtractCfg` | optional | — |
| `summarize` | `SummarizeCfg` | optional | — |
| `store` | `StoreCfg` | optional | — |
| `cards` | `CardsCfg` | optional | — |
| `workspace` | `WorkspaceCfg` | optional | — |

## `[repo]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | optional | Defaults to the directory basename. |
| `root` | `path` | optional | Repo root; default = the toml's dir. |

## `[extract]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kinds` | `list` | optional | Impl kinds tried in order: "manifest" | "treesitter" | "lsp". |
| `lsp_server` | `string` | optional | Server command for the lsp adapter (per-language later). |

## `[summarize]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `string` | optional | "template" (deterministic, default) | "llm". |
| `provider` | `string` | optional | Provider id for the llm adapter; key resolves via secrets chain. |
| `model` | `string` | optional | — |

## `[store]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kind` | `string` | optional | — |
| `path` | `path` | optional | L2 index path — rebuildable, gitignored. |

## `[cards]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dir` | `path` | optional | Committed artifacts dir: index.yaml + modules/\*.yaml. |

## `[workspace]`

| field | type | required | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `roots` | `Vec<PathBuf>` | optional | Sibling repo roots indexed together. |
| `resolve_git_deps` | `bool` | optional | Resolve `git = ".../org/repo"` manifest deps to siblings. |

## Constraints

* `queue = "all"` rejects `cancel_running = true` at load —
  killing a run would silently drop a promised commit.
* `runner.kind` and `trigger.kind`/`status.kind` resolve to impl
  crates; unknown kinds fail at `kuda doctor`/startup.
* `deny_unknown_fields`: typos in field names fail the load.

# Explanation: architecture

## Tiered memory, not one big summary

A monolithic repo summary fails twice: too coarse to plan with, or
too big for context. kuda produces a hierarchy agents zoom into:

* **L0 — repo card** (`index.yaml`, ~1k tokens): purpose, module
  map, entry points, build/test commands. Always-loadable.
* **L1 — module cards** (`modules/*.yaml`): API surface, deps,
  invariants, `verify:` file list. Fetched when planning.
* **L2 — symbol/dep graph** (`index.sqlite`): symbol -> file:line
  and dep edges both directions. Queried, not loaded.
* **L3 — source**: the code. Memory indexes it; never replaces it.

## Provenance is the staleness model

Every card records `{files, content_hash, commit_sha}`.
`kuda status` diffs the recorded sha against HEAD — drift is a
property of the data, not a promise in prose. `sync` regenerates
only cards whose `files` changed.

## Ports and adapters

Every concern is a trait crate + adapter crates (ADR-0001):

* extract: `manifest` (free, no parser) -> `treesitter`
  (grammar+query data) -> `lsp` (cross-file refs where a server
  exists)
* summarize: `template` (deterministic default) | `llm` (opt-in
  prose — provider key stays in env/keyring)
* store: `sqlite` (rebuildable, gitignored)
* serve: `cli` | `mcp`

## Language as data

Per-language knowledge — grammar refs, symbol queries, manifest
kinds — lives in `data/langs/*`, not in extractor code. A new
language is a data change; the engine's vocabulary is fixed.

## Trust model

Cards end with `verify:` — the files an agent should open before
acting on the card. Memory is a hypothesis that narrows the search
space; the code remains the only truth.

url: /kuda/explanation/release-model.md
---
# The release model

kuda releases itself — there is no hosted CI and no release tool
in the loop. Two deliberate phases:

## Phase 1 — the explicit seed

`kuda deploy release` runs once, by hand: it reads cargo metadata,
topologically orders the workspace's path-dependency graph,
`cargo publish`es every member, tags `{repo}-v{version}`, and pushes
the tag.

Why explicit? Publishing is the **only irreversible step** in the
whole system. Queues, runs, and statuses are all idempotent and
local; a crate version on crates.io is forever. Everything else in
kuda fires on push — the seed doesn't. (`--dry-run` prints the
order and tag without touching anything.)

## Phase 2 — push-driven forever after

From then on a release is *just another kuda job*: a push to `main`
hits the webhook, queues latest-wins, and runs `scripts/release.sh`
in a detached worktree under the shell runner.

The script:

1. diffs crate paths since the last `kuda-v*` tag
2. `cargo set-version --bump patch` on touched crates only (the cli
   republishes on any change — it's the install artifact)
3. `cargo publish`es them in dep order
4. tags `kuda-vX.Y.Z`, builds host-arch binaries with `cargo dist`,
   uploads to a GitHub Release via `gh`

The 5-minute sleep at the top isn't a hack — it's the debounce
window. Combined with `queue = "latest"` + `cancel_running`, rapid
push bursts collapse to one release of the newest sha; killed runs
get an honest "cancelled" status.

## Why this shape

* **No release-plz / GHA**: the point of the project is that CI is a
  local loop — depending on hosted CI to ship it would be
  self-defeating. `release.sh` is deliberately boring bash so it can
  run as a plain `cmd` under `runner.kind = "shell"`.
* **Latest-wins, not `all`**: a release that misses an intermediate
  push loses nothing — the tag lands on HEAD, which contains
  everything. `queue = "all"` is for pipelines where each sha's run
  is individually meaningful.
* **Explicit over automatic**: a wrong tag or half-published
  workspace is far worse than a delayed release; the boundary sits
  exactly at irreversibility.

Host prerequisites: `cargo-edit`, `cargo-dist`, `gh`, and
`CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` (env → keyring → env file). Multi-arch
binaries arrive when the remote-runner pair lands — see TODO.

# kuda vs the alternatives

## vs grep + re-read every session

|                       | grep/ripgrep          | kuda                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------- |
| find a symbol         | fast, per-query       | fast — plus kind + card    |
| "what depends on X"   | manual, cross-repo pain | one query                |
| overall comprehension | none                  | L0 card in ~1k tokens      |
| freshness             | always current        | provenance-checked         |
| doc/comment mentions  | same grep             | unified `refs --docs`      |

## vs embeddings / RAG

|                       | RAG store             | kuda                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------- |
| fuzzy semantic lookup | strong                | (optional store adapter later)|
| dep graph, provenance | weak                  | first-class                |
| staleness             | opaque                | explicit sha/hash diff     |
| determinism           | model-dependent       | `template` = deterministic |

## vs LSP alone

|                       | LSP                   | kuda                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------- | -------------------------- |
| cross-file refs       | strong (per language) | `lsp` adapter reuses them     |
| needs a running server| yes                   | only for the `lsp` tier    |
| prose/cards           | none                  | L1/L0 artifacts            |
| persistence           | session-scoped        | committed + rebuildable    |

Trade-off: kuda adds an index step and committed artifacts — the
payoff is that "overall comprehension" becomes a fixed ~1k-token
load instead of a per-session expedition.

# Getting started

Pick by what you need to do.

* **Tutorials** (learn): [first-run](tutorials/first-run.md)
* **How-to** (tasks): [multi-repo](how-to/multi-repo.md) ·
  [mcp](how-to/mcp.md) ·
  [llm summarizer](how-to/llm-summarizer.md)
* **Reference** (lookup): [cli](reference/cli.md) ·
  [config](reference/config.md) ·
  [crate api](reference/crate-api.md)
* **Explanation** (why): [architecture](explanation/architecture.md) ·
  [release model](explanation/release-model.md) ·
  [comparison](comparison.md) — vs grep / RAG

Install:

```sh
cargo install --git https://github.com/9aia/kuda kuda
```

First index:

```sh
cd your-repo
kuda init    # detect languages -> kuda.toml + .kuda/
kuda sync    # incremental index -> .kuda/ artifacts
kuda status  # provenance vs HEAD
kuda map     # the L0 card — what agents load first
```
